plan: [ Three-player second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values (0–49). In such auctions, truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others’ behavior since you pay the second-highest bid if you win. There’s no history to learn from and only one round, so no benefit to shading or signaling. To maximize expected profit, I will bid exactly my private value of $32.0, aligned with the 0.1 increment rule. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid your true value: overbidding can lead to negative payoff if you win and pay above your value; underbidding risks losing profitable wins. With 1 round and no exploitable history, maximizing expected profit means bidding exactly $9. If I win, I pay the second-highest bid, which is ≤ 9, ensuring non-negative profit; if I lose, payoff is zero. Thus, truthful bidding is optimal for long-run and this single round. ]

[ This is a 3-bidder sealed-bid second-price auction. The dominant strategy is to bid my true private value, because the price paid is the second-highest bid. Any bid above my value risks winning at a price exceeding my value; any bid below risks losing when winning would have been profitable. There’s no useful history (single round) and values are i.i.d. each round. With value = 46, bidding 46 maximizes expected profit while handling tie-breaking randomly without downside. ]
